deep.reconstruction:
This is not a page of mathematics. It is the inside front cover, or first leaf, of a bound notebook. The deliberate writing on it is:
(a) An ownership inscription in ink, upper right: 'Professor David Hilbert. Augustastr. 4.'
(b) A date in ink, lower right: '12 November 1892.'
(c) A faint pencil note, upper left: 'Für Beer 1, 23, 27, 29, 37, 45' (reading uncertain). These look like page or item numbers set aside for, or referring to, someone or something called 'Beer'. They are possibly a later cataloguer's or reader's note.
(d) The library stamp of the Niedersächsische Staats- u. Universitätsbibliothek Göttingen.

Date and address context: in 1892 Hilbert was still in Königsberg. He became extraordinarius there in 1892, married Käthe Jerosch in October 1892, and only moved to Göttingen in 1895. 'Augustastr. 4' is therefore most plausibly a Königsberg address, not his later Göttingen house in Wilhelm-Weber-Str. This dating fits the notebook being begun right after his marriage and promotion.

Faint text from the facing or following leaf is visible through the paper. It is not part of this page proper, and the reading is partial and uncertain. It seems to contain a number-theoretic argument roughly as follows:
- If the degree of some substitution or field is the prime p, then a polynomial satisfies φ(x) ≡ x^p + h x (mod p).
- From φ(x+1) ≡ φ(x) (my reading of 'φ(x)+1 ≡ φ(x)...') it follows easily that h ≡ −1 (mod p).
- Hence φ(x) ≡ x^p − x (mod p) has only distinct roots ('lauter verschiedene Wurzeln'), and its discriminant is not divisible by p.

In modern terms, this is the statement that a polynomial of degree p invariant (mod p) under x → x+1 is x^p − x plus a constant. Then x^p − x = ∏_{a∈F_p}(x − a) is separable mod p, since its derivative is −1. This is the kind of residue-field lemma that occurs in Hilbert's 1894 work on ramification in Galois number fields, and it is reminiscent of what was later called Artin–Schreier.

Two further show-through passages are non-mathematical in form:
- One concerns constructing an 'idealen Wahrscheinlichkeitsapparat (Würfel?)', i.e. finding a mechanism in which pure chance reigns, which 'runs contrary' to something. This is a philosophical remark on probability.
- The other concerns 'eine Theorie des Rechnens' and its advantages.

None of this can be properly reconstructed from this image. It belongs to the next leaf.
errors: No derivation is written on this page itself, so there is nothing to check.
The show-through argument (φ ≡ x^p + h x, invariance under x → x+1 gives h ≡ −1, so x^p − x is separable mod p) is correct as far as it can be read.

checkable.asserts: x^p − x is invariant under x → x+1 modulo p (shown for p = 5)
x^p − x splits into p distinct linear factors over F_p (shown for p = 7)
